chunks: My father narrated to us, may God be pleased with him, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Imran al-Ash'ari, from Ali ibn Muhammad, from a man, from Suleiman ibn Ziyad al-Minqari, from Amr ibn Shimr, from Isma'il al-Sadi, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Sabit al-Qurashi, from Jabir ibn Abdullah al-Ansari.

Regarding the saying of God, the Mighty and Majestic, narrating about Joseph: 'I saw eleven stars and the sun and the moon: I saw them prostrate themselves to me.' He then spoke about the naming of the stars: They are Al-Tariq, Jirban, Al-Ziyal, Dhul-Kanfan, Dhul-Qur', Qabis, Was'sab, Amudan and Faylaq, Misbah, Al-Darur, Al-Diya' and Al-Nur, meaning the sun and the moon. And all these stars encompass the sky.

key_terms.الضِّيَاءُ وَالنُّورُ: Al-Diya' and Al-Nur (names referring to the sun and moon)

ai.seo_question: What are the names of the eleven stars that Prophet Joseph saw in his dream according to Shia tradition?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records this narration to provide a specific cosmological identification for the 'eleven stars' mentioned in Surah Yusuf, listing their traditional Arabic names such as Al-Tariq and Jarran. This commentary reflects the Shia scholarly tradition of linking Quranic narratives with detailed astronomical knowledge, interpreting the prostration as a literal celestial event involving these specific fixed stars and the sun and moon.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 11-1 (The compiler of the book narrated) that his father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar quoted Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Imran al-Ash’ari, on the authority of Ali ibn Muhammad, on the authority of Suleiman ibn Zyad al-Minqari, on the authority of Amr ibn Shimr, on the authority of Isma’il ibn al-Sadi, on the authority of Abdul Rahman ibn Sabit al-Qurashi, on the authority of Jabir ibn Abdullah al-Ansari, “Regarding what God said about Joseph (MGB)we read the following in the Holy Quran, ‘I did see eleven stars and the sun and the moon: I saw them prostrate themselves to me![12:4]’

Then he started to name those stars: that were Al-Tariq, Jirban, Al-Zial, Zul-Kanafan, Zul-Qar’e, Qabis, Vas’sab, Amoodan, Faylaq, Misbah, Al-Zaruh, Al-Zia’e and Al-Nur implying the sun and the moon. All the stars are encompassed by the sky.”
